narrative: The model estimated a 39% probability that you would become a bad credit risk. Although that is below 50%, it is above the bank’s approval threshold, so your application was denied. The most influential factor was your savings information, and it actually worked in your favour, lowering the estimated risk. Your savings were recorded as unknown/none, which is relatively common—about one third of approved applicants have the same—so this was not treated as a major warning sign. The next most important factor was that you already have an installment plan with a bank. This pushed the estimate toward bad credit and was the clearest risk-increasing factor in the top three; only about 9% of approved applicants have this. Third, your checking account status was recorded as none. That also reduced the estimated risk and is common among approved applicants. Overall, the helpful signals from your savings and checking-account information were not enough to offset the risk raised by the existing bank installment plan and the rest of your profile, including a 28-month request versus about 19 months for approved applicants and a much larger loan amount. To proceed, ask the bank what conditions would support reconsideration, clarify your savings records, avoid adding new installment commitments, and consider a smaller or shorter loan.
